# 1.34.0: More providers, your own server, model lists that load again, new default models

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are. Going back to 1.33
with the button in Settings → About keeps your Venice and OpenRouter keys.

## Providers

- **Keys from more services.** Besides Venice and OpenRouter, the program now works directly with
  OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, xAI (Grok), DeepSeek, Kimi (Moonshot), Mistral,
  Z.ai (GLM), Qwen (Alibaba) and Groq. Claude speaks its own protocol here, with thinking, tool
  calls, pictures and PDF files, not a compatibility layer.
- **Your own server.** A reseller or gateway with an OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible API is added
  by its address (base URL). The program finds the API root, with or without `/v1`, and the
  protocols it speaks, without running a model. The address must use https, except for this
  computer. Claude models go through the native protocol when the server has it.
- **A new Add key window.** The service is chosen from a list, and the program picks it by itself
  for keys it recognizes (Anthropic, OpenRouter, xAI, Groq, Gemini, OpenAI project keys). The
  window shows the address the key will be sent to. When a key is refused, the reason is short
  and honest: "not accepted" only when the service says so, and "access denied" when the service
  refuses this network or country.
- **Keys sold as a package of tokens.** Set the limit in the key's menu (Token limit), and the
  program counts the tokens it uses and shows what's left on the Keys & spending page and in the
  balance tooltip. The count is the program's own: a reseller may charge some models at a higher
  rate.
- **Spending for every service.** Services that don't report the price of a reply get an
  estimate from the tokens used and the public price list of OpenRouter, so the spending chart
  and the limits keep working. The price list is fetched only when you use such a service.
- **Model picker.** The provider column scrolls, services with keys come first, your servers are
  listed by name, and **Add key** under a service without a key opens the window on that service.
- Pictures and reading web pages still work through Venice. Web search works through Venice or
  OpenRouter: a conversation that runs elsewhere searches through them when you have their key.

## Model lists

- **A list that failed to load loads again.** When a service refuses to give its model list
  (for example, OpenRouter answering "Access Denied" because of the country), the picker says why
  in plain words and offers **Retry**. Opening the picker again or clicking the service also
  retries. Before, the first refusal stayed until the program was restarted.
- Models that were already loaded stay on screen while a new attempt runs.
- Lists load side by side and each waits at most 30 seconds, so a slow service no longer holds
  the others.

## New default models

| Task | Model | Thinking |
|---|---|---|
| Chat, light | Claude Haiku 5.5 | medium |
| Chat, heavy | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | low |
| Router | DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 | off |
| Agent, fast | DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 | medium |
| Agent, light | Claude Haiku 5.5 | low |
| Agent, heavy | Grok 4.7 | medium |
| Chat titles | DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 | off |
| Summary | Claude Haiku 5.5 | low |
| Web search | Auto | |

- A slot that still holds the default of 1.33 switches to the new one once. Anything you chose
  yourself stays as it is.
- New profiles start the chat on **Auto**.
- The same model works with any service: with only an OpenRouter or Anthropic key, the slots
  move there with the same models once the service's list loads.
- A thinking level a model doesn't have becomes the nearest one it has (the lower one on a tie),
  not the model's own default. OpenRouter models now show the levels they really accept.
- The **Auto** icon is now a pair of scales: the router weighs each request between the light
  and the heavy model.

## Fixes

- A reply sent again without its thinking level no longer loses its token count and cost.
- When a model is overloaded, the replacement comes from the same service. Before, a request to
  another service could be retried with a Venice model.
